paras: The killing of Henry Mitchell was the fatal shooting of a Black workman during a row between white and Black workmen at the Ohio Valley cement mill, six miles from Jeffersonville, Indiana, on the night of December 24, 1881. Mitchell was shot by a local man named Long, who escaped. Newspapers from West Virginia to Minnesota and Mississippi carried a brief wire dispatch about it among the many Christmas crimes of that year.

On Saturday night, Christmas eve, a quarrel broke out at the cement mill "between a lot of white and negro workmen." According to the Jeffersonville dispatch, Mitchell had a shotgun and "attempted to use it upon one Long, who lives in that vicinity." Long then got a gun of his own and, while Mitchell was threatening to shoot him, shot him in the breast, killing him almost instantly. This version is the only one in the coverage, and it does not say who started the row, whether Long worked at the mill, or what race he was.
Long escaped after the shooting. No report of an arrest, inquest or trial appears in the coverage.

The story reached the press as a single Jeffersonville wire dispatch, dated December 25 in the Memphis Daily Appeal and December 26 in the two Wheeling papers. The Appeal ran it as "Row with Fatal Results" in a long column of "Christmas Crimes," and the Wheeling Register headed it "Killed in a Row." The Wheeling Daily Intelligencer printed the same text under "Got the Drop on Him," a headline that cast the killing as the shooter outdrawing an armed man. All three gave the claim that Mitchell had threatened Long as fact, without naming a source.

Elsewhere the item shrank to a single line in crime digests, such as the St. Paul Daily Globe's "Hy. Mitchell, negro" and a New Jersey weekly's "fight between white and colored men." The Mower County Transcript in Minnesota listed it among the season's "rows and affrays among gangs of workmen," and the Weekly Clarion in Mississippi repeated the line in mid-January. None of these papers commented on the killing, and no Indiana paper's account was found.

reader.title: Killing of Henry Mitchell
bases: The only detailed account describes a row between white and Black workmen at a cement mill that ended when one man, Long, shot Mitchell, not a group attack, lynching or labor action (A1, A3).
Every report repeats or condenses one Jeffersonville wire dispatch (A1, A3, A4), and the shorter items (A2, A5, A6, A7) add nothing independent; no local paper, inquest or arrest report was found.

accounts.label: Jeffersonville wire dispatch
accounts.gist: A row between white and Black workmen at the cement mill ended with Long shooting Mitchell, who had first tried to use a shotgun on him and was threatening him when shot; Long escaped. No witness or official is named as the source of this version.

framing.detail: The Memphis Appeal ran it as 'Row with Fatal Results' in a 'Christmas Crimes' column and the Wheeling Register as 'Killed in a Row', both giving the shooter's justification as fact.
The Wheeling Daily Intelligencer headed the same text 'Got the Drop on Him,' casting the killing as the shooter getting the better of an armed man.
Digests and weeklies cut it to one line among holiday crimes; the Mower County Transcript filed it under rows 'among gangs of workmen'.

conflicts.note: Dateline difference only; all versions place the row on Saturday night, December 24.
The digest wording drops 'workmen'; not a substantive conflict.

record_check.dossier: A single shooting by one man (Long) after a row between white and Black workmen; no mob attack is described. 'other' (workplace dispute) fits better.

sources.note: Jeffersonville dispatch dated Dec. 25 in a 'Christmas Crimes' column: row at the Ohio Valley cement mill between white and Black workmen; Long shot Henry Mitchell, who had a shotgun, and escaped. Same column has an unrelated Jeffersonville beating (Alexander Gilbert).
quotes: A row at the Ohio Valley cement mill, six miles from this city, Saturday night, between a lot of white and negro workmen, resulted in the killing of Henry Mitchell, colored.
Long procured a gun afterward and, while the negro was threatening to shoot him, shot the negro in the breast, killing him almost instantly. He escaped.
